name: ELVES
tagline: A Local Volume survey of satellites around Milky Way-mass host galaxies.
description: ELVES is a survey of satellite systems around Milky Way-mass hosts in the Local Volume.
overview: ELVES targets the satellite populations of Milky Way-mass host galaxies in the Local Volume.
This page will collect the survey description, associated papers, public catalogs, imaging products, distance measurements, and citation guidance.
motivation: The survey is intended to support comparisons between satellite populations in nearby Milky Way-mass environments and models of dwarf-galaxy formation.
Future data releases will document the selection, measurements, and recommended use of the public products.

name: ELVES-Dwarf
tagline: ELVES-Dwarf extends the ELVES survey family into the dwarf-host regime, providing a systematic view of satellite populations around dwarf host galaxies in the nearby Universe.
description: ELVES-Dwarf is a survey of satellite systems around primarily isolated dwarf hosts in the Local Volume.

figure.alt: Map of the ELVES-Dwarf systems in the Local Volume. Hosts are placed at their distances from the Milky Way, with circle sizes scaled by virial radius. Confirmed satellites and unconfirmed candidates appear at their projected separations and are colored by stellar mass.
figure.caption: The ELVES-Dwarf systems across the Local Volume. Each host is placed at its distance from the Milky Way; the angle is chosen only for demonstration purposes. Circle size scales with virial radius, while satellites and candidates are shown at their projected separations.

question: Do dwarf galaxies, 10 to 1000 times smaller than the Milky Way, have satellite systems of their own?
results: The ELVES-Dwarf survey addresses this question by constructing the **first large, homogeneous, distance-confirmed sample of satellites around dwarf hosts**. The survey targets 39 primarily isolated dwarf galaxies in the Local Volume, spanning host stellar masses of \(10^8\text{--}10^{10}\,M_\odot\).

We search the hosts out to its projected virial radius using 155 square degrees of Legacy Surveys imaging, and measure their distances using surface brightness fluctuation (SBF). We have identified 39 confirmed satellites, and the survey is typically complete down to \(M_\star \gtrsim 10^{5.7}\,M_\odot\).

The satellite populations show substantial diversity from host to host. The satellite abundance, stellar-mass functions, and radial distribution are broadly consistent with theoretical predictions. However, ELVES-Dwarf satellites have a substantially lower quenched fraction than satellites around Milky Way-mass hosts, suggesting that the weaker environments of dwarf galaxies are less efficient at shutting down star formation in their satellites.

motivation: Dwarf-host satellite systems provide a lower-mass comparison point for understanding how satellite populations vary with host mass and environment.
citation: Please cite the full ELVES-Dwarf survey paper and any relevant science papers when using these data products.

name: ELVES-Field
tagline: A Local Volume survey of dwarf galaxies in the field.
description: ELVES-Field is a survey of dwarf galaxies in the Local Volume field.
overview: ELVES-Field focuses on dwarf galaxies in the Local Volume field.
This page will collect the field dwarf catalog, distance measurements, imaging products, papers, data access notes, and citation guidance.
motivation: Field dwarf galaxies provide an environmental reference for interpreting satellites around more massive and lower-mass hosts.
Future releases will describe the catalog construction, measurement products, and appropriate citation practices.
